result.title: From Dense to Sparse: Morton-Ordered Sparse Mapping for Efficient 3D Mesh Generation
result.summary: Unified 3D understanding and generation require compact sequences preserving spatial structure. Dense grids yield long sequences, while serialization can separate spatial neighbors. We propose Sparse Proximity Aware Compression (SPAC), a shared sparse SDF vocabulary combining sparse encoding with reversible spatial merging. A Sparse SDF VQ-VAE quantizes near-surface features while retaining explicit coordinates, using reconstruction supervision for surface fidelity and detail. 3D Byte-Pair Encoding (3D-BPE) merges recurring face-adjacent patterns using relative offsets before serialization. Macro tokens expand exactly into leaf tokens and coordinates. After Morton serialization, a shared LLM reads geometry for captioning and predicts tokens that decode into meshes for text-conditioned generation. With fixed geometry, architecture, and band width in voxels, sparse encoder cost grows approximately quadratically with resolution. 3D-BPE reduces mean complete LLM sequence length by 45.4 percent, including coordinates, text, and control tokens. SPAC achieves strong results in both 3D captioning and text-conditioned mesh generation. Ablations show gains over leaf tokens and Morton 1D-BPE in both tasks. The project page at https://yangjj007.github.io/spac/ .

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SPAC：用稀疏 SDF VQ-VAE 量化近表面特征并保留显式坐标，再用 3D-BPE 合并面相邻宏 token，经 Morton 序列化后由共享 LLM 完成 3D 描述与文本条件网格生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作重心是 3D 网格的稀疏 token 化与序列压缩，属于 3D 生成与表示效率，未涉及 VLM 推理状态生成、证据获取、停止决策或 latent 内容被答案使用等主线问题，也未提供可具体核查的借用线索。
